# Command reference

Every backend command the frontend can call: **142 commands** in 26 modules. The desktop app calls them through Tauri's `invoke()`; a browser calls the ones marked **Browser** through `POST /api/rpc/{command}` (see {doc}`/developer/browser-server`). Arguments are sent as a JSON object with camelCase keys. A failed command rejects with `{ error, message }`.

Browser-callable: **111** of 142. The rest read or write files on the host machine, manage the host (voice model downloads, network settings, account switching), or are not needed in a browser yet.

(auth)=
## auth

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs`

### `auth_status`

Whether any account exists, who may sign up, and which account this window is acting as (plus the admin it is acting for, if any).

No arguments.

Returns `Result<AuthStatus, MythicError>`

### `auth_register`

Creates an account. The first one becomes the admin. The new account
becomes the one the desktop acts as.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `username` | `String` |
| `passphrase` | `String` |

Returns `Result<AccountCreated, MythicError>`

### `auth_login`

Signs the desktop window in as an account, checking its passphrase.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `username` | `String` |
| `passphrase` | `String` |

Returns `Result<UserInfo, MythicError>`

### `auth_switch_to`

The admin, sitting at the host machine, acts as any account without its
passphrase (to help someone or check what they see), and can return to the
admin account the same way. Desktop only: it is not reachable from the
browser.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `userId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<UserInfo, MythicError>`

### `auth_logout`

Signs the desktop window out. Until someone signs in again, account-owned data is not reachable.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `auth_reset_with_recovery`

Sets a new passphrase using the account's recovery key, signs every other session out, and issues a fresh recovery key.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `username` | `String` |
| `recoveryKey` | `String` |
| `newPassphrase` | `String` |

Returns `Result<AccountCreated, MythicError>`

### `auth_change_passphrase`

Changes the signed-in account's passphrase after checking the current one.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `currentPassphrase` | `String` |
| `newPassphrase` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `auth_set_signup_mode`

Admin only: chooses whether anyone can sign up (`open`) or only the admin creates accounts (`admin_only`).

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `SignupMode` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `auth_list_users`

Admin only: lists every account.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<Vec<UserInfo>, MythicError>`

### `auth_create_user`

Admin adds a member with a temporary passphrase they must replace on
first sign-in. The desktop keeps acting as the admin.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `username` | `String` |
| `temporaryPassphrase` | `String` |

Returns `Result<AccountCreated, MythicError>`

### `auth_delete_user`

Admin only: deletes an account together with its characters, chats, memories, providers and stored files.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `userId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

(character-state)=
## character_state

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/character_state.rs`

### `get_character_state` — **Browser**

Returns the current emotional state for a character in a conversation.
Returns `None` if no state has been recorded yet (first turn).

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |
| `conversationId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Option<CharacterState>, MythicError>`

### `upsert_character_state` — **Browser**

Upserts the emotional state for a character in a conversation.
All integer axes are clamped to [0, 100].

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `mood` | `i32` |
| `trust` | `i32` |
| `arousal` | `i32` |
| `dominantEmotion` | `String` |
| `stateSummary` | `String` |

Returns `Result<CharacterState, MythicError>`

### `set_message_emotional_snapshot` — **Browser**

Freezes an emotional-state snapshot (one entry per character, keyed by
character id) onto a specific message's metadata, so its EmotionHUD pill
keeps showing what each character felt *at that point in the story*
instead of whatever `character_states` holds right now. `states` is
passed through as raw JSON rather than a typed map — the backend never
reads its shape, only stores and returns it verbatim to the frontend.
Uses `DynamicJson`, not a bare `serde_json::Value` param — see its doc
comment in `models::mod` for why (the same infinite-recursion crash
`JsonValue` was built to avoid).

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `messageId` | `String` |
| `states` | `DynamicJson` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

(chatattachments)=
## chat/attachments

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/chat/attachments.rs`

### `upload_message_attachment`

Copies a user-picked image file (an absolute path from the frontend's
file dialog) into `app_data_dir/attachments/`, so it can be attached to
a chat message and later resolved via `crate::error::resolve_within`.

Unlike `upload_character_avatar`, this preserves the source file's real
extension instead of hardcoding `.png` — the extension is how
`mime_type_for_extension` (and, on replay, `load_message_images`) knows
what MIME type to hand the provider.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `filePath` | `String` |

Returns `Result<crate::models::conversation::MessageAttachment, MythicError>`

### `upload_message_attachment_bytes`

Same as `upload_message_attachment`, but for an image pasted directly
from the clipboard (e.g. a screenshot) — there's no source file on disk
to read, just raw bytes and the clipboard blob's MIME type from the
frontend's `paste` event.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `bytes` | `Vec<u8>` |
| `extension` | `String` |

Returns `Result<crate::models::conversation::MessageAttachment, MythicError>`

(chatretry)=
## chat/retry

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/chat/retry.rs`

### `retry_failed_message` — **Browser**

Retries a failed message by reusing the existing user message already in the DB.
Cleans up the empty/failed assistant placeholder from the previous attempt,
creates a fresh one, and re-triggers LLM generation. This avoids duplicating
the user message in both the UI and database.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `userMessageId` | `String` |
| `model` | `Option<String>` |
| `systemPrompt` | `Option<String>` |
| `streaming` | `Option<bool>` |
| `postHistoryInstructions` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<SendMessageResult, MythicError>`

### `regenerate_message` — **Browser**

Regenerates the AI response for a given message by re-running generation
from the same parent point in the conversation tree.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `messageId` | `String` |
| `model` | `Option<String>` |
| `systemPrompt` | `Option<String>` |
| `streaming` | `Option<bool>` |
| `postHistoryInstructions` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<SendMessageResult, MythicError>`

### `cancel_generation` — **Browser**

Cancels the in-flight generation for a conversation, if any.

Aborts the generation task and, for a streaming generation, persists
whatever content had already streamed so the response isn't lost just
because it was stopped early — a cancelled message is not the same as a
failed one. Emits a "cancelled" chat-stream event (not "done" or "error")
so the frontend can finalize the UI without triggering the auto-memory-
extraction/emotion-update pipelines that "done" runs, since those
shouldn't fire over content the user explicitly cut off.

A no-op (not an error) if nothing is in flight for this conversation —
e.g. the user clicked Stop just as generation finished on its own.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

(chatsend)=
## chat/send

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/chat/send.rs`

### `send_message` — **Browser**

Sends a user message and streams the AI response back.

This is the primary chat endpoint. It:
1. Saves the user message to the database
2. Builds the full prompt from character data + conversation history
3. Streams the response from the active LLM provider
4. Saves the completed AI response to the database

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `content` | `String` |
| `model` | `Option<String>` |
| `systemPrompt` | `Option<String>` |
| `streaming` | `Option<bool>` |
| `postHistoryInstructions` | `Option<String>` |
| `attachments` | `Option<Vec<crate::models::conversation::MessageAttachment>>` |

Returns `Result<SendMessageResult, MythicError>`

(data-backup)=
## data_backup

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/data_backup.rs`

### `export_data_backup`

Exports the entire datastore to a new timestamped file under
`<app_data_dir>/backups/` and returns its absolute path, so the frontend
can show it to the user (and offer to reveal it in the file manager).

No arguments.

Returns `Result<String, MythicError>`

### `import_data_backup`

Imports a `.surql` backup file (produced by [`export_data_backup`] or the
automatic rolling backup) into the current datastore. Existing records
with the same ID are left as-is by SurrealDB's import (it replays
`CREATE`/`UPSERT`-shaped statements, which don't overwrite silently) —
this is meant for restoring into a fresh/empty datastore, not merging
into one with unrelated existing data.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `filePath` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `list_data_backups`

Lists the backup files in the app's `backups/` folder, newest first.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<Vec<BackupFileInfo>, MythicError>`

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/embeddings.rs`

### `get_embedding_index_status` — **Browser**

Returns the current state of the vector embedding index.

The frontend uses this to show how many messages are embedded,
which model was used, and whether a rebuild is needed.

### `rebuild_embedding_index` — **Browser**

Rebuilds the embedding index by deleting existing embeddings and
re-embedding all user/assistant messages with the specified model.

Returns the updated `EmbeddingIndexStatus` when done.

|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `Option<String>` |
| `embeddingModel` | `String` |

Returns `Result<EmbeddingIndexStatus, MythicError>`

### `backfill_missing_embeddings` — **Browser**

Finds messages that don't have embeddings yet and embeds them in batches.
This is a non-destructive catch-up — it only fills gaps without touching
existing embeddings. Designed to run on conversation load or periodically.

Returns the updated `EmbeddingIndexStatus` when done.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<EmbeddingIndexStatus, MythicError>`

(import)=
## import

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/import.rs`

### `import_character_card`

Imports a character from a PNG file containing embedded Character Card V2 data.

Flow:
1. User selects a PNG via the file dialog
2. Read the PNG bytes
3. Extract the "chara" tEXt chunk and decode base64
4. Parse as CharacterCardV2 JSON
5. Save the character to the database
6. Copy the PNG as the character's avatar

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `filePath` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `import_persona_card`

Imports a persona from a PNG file containing embedded Character Card V2
data — the same "chara" tEXt-chunk convention as `import_character_card`,
just landing in the `personas` table and its own `personas/` avatar
subdirectory instead of `characters`/`avatars/`.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `filePath` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Persona, MythicError>`

### `get_avatar_path`

Serves an avatar image from the app data directory.
Returns the absolute path to the avatar file for the frontend to load.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `avatarRelative` | `String` |

Returns `Result<String, MythicError>`

(logs)=
## logs

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/logs.rs`

### `get_backend_logs`

Returns the last `lines` (default 1000, capped at `MAX_LINES`) lines of
the persisted backend log file, oldest first within that window. Empty
string (not an error) if the file doesn't exist yet — e.g. right after a
fresh install before anything's been logged.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `lines` | `Option<u32>` |

Returns `Result<String, MythicError>`

### `get_backend_logs_page`

Returns one page of backend log lines read backward from `cursor` (a byte
offset into the log file; omit to start at the end — the newest lines).
Used by the Logging tab's viewer to load the file incrementally as the
user scrolls up, rather than reading it in full up front: only a bounded
window at the tail is read per call, growing just enough to cover the
requested `limit` lines.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `cursor` | `Option<u32>` |
| `limit` | `Option<u32>` |

Returns `Result<LogPage, MythicError>`

### `get_backend_log_path`

Absolute path to the backend log file — shown in the Logging tab so the
user can locate it directly (e.g. to attach to a bug report) without
going through Export.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<String, MythicError>`

(npc)=
## npc

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/npc.rs`

### `list_conversation_npcs` — **Browser**

Lists the auto-detected cast currently in a conversation — both
`role = 'transient'` (just spoke for the first time, not yet confirmed
significant) and `role = 'npc'` (crossed the two-pass debounce and got a
real profile) members, plus already-promoted-to-gallery ones, since
promotion only changes `origin`, not cast membership. Transients are
included (not just 'npc') so a character who's clearly speaking and
developing a real identity doesn't just vanish from this panel while
waiting on the background debounce — the frontend badges them as
"Unconfirmed" rather than hiding them outright.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Vec<Character>, MythicError>`

### `promote_npc_to_gallery` — **Browser**

Promotes an auto-generated NPC into a real, standalone Gallery character
(`origin: 'npc' -> 'gallery'`). No cast/memory data moves — the NPC's
memories were already keyed by its own real `character_id` from creation,
and it keeps its existing `conversation_characters` row (still shows in
this conversation's cast) while now also being independently listable
and startable as a solo chat from the Gallery.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `confirm_npc` — **Browser**

Manually promotes an auto-detected NPC from `role: 'transient'`
("Unconfirmed" in the UI) straight to `role: 'npc'`, skipping the
automatic two-pass detector debounce (`pipeline::run_npc_detection`).
That debounce is entirely invisible to the user — a character can speak
repeatedly and be directly addressed without the periodic detection
pass ever happening to re-flag them as recurring, leaving them stuck as
"Unconfirmed" indefinitely with no visible reason and, until now, no way
to override it.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `characterId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `mark_npc_reviewed` — **Browser**

Marks an NPC's auto-generated profile as reviewed — clears the "new
profile" half of the needs-attention indicator's condition.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `refresh_character_profile` — **Browser**

Refreshes a character's description/personality/scenario against how
they've actually appeared in this conversation — canon facts (settled,
character-level truth) plus recent dialogue (voice/tone anchor), with
the character's own current profile passed in so the model refines
rather than reinvents (and knows to disregard the "just spoke for the
first time" placeholder as if it were empty). Used by both the manual
"Refresh from Story" button and the automatic still-placeholder trigger
in the NPC detection pipeline.

If this character appears in more than just this one conversation, the
card is deliberately left untouched — see `ProfileRefreshResult::scope`.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `// User-editable override from Settings > Prompts > Character Profile
    // Refresh. `None` (e.g. the automatic pipeline trigger, which has no
    // frontend settings to read) falls back to the built-in default.
    systemPrompt` | `Option<String>,` |

Returns `Result<ProfileRefreshResult, MythicError>`

### `generate_npc_portrait` — **Browser**

Generates a portrait for an NPC via the configured image provider,
framed from its auto-generated description. Silently skips — returns the
character unchanged, no error — if no image provider is configured; an
auto-approved placeholder gradient standing in for a face would be worse
than no portrait at all.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `autoApprove` | `bool` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `approve_npc_portrait` — **Browser**

Approves a pending NPC portrait (`portrait_status -> 'approved'`) — the
avatar image itself is left unchanged.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `reject_npc_portrait` — **Browser**

Rejects a pending NPC portrait — clears the avatar entirely (back to the
initial-circle placeholder) rather than leaving a rejected image in place.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `get_cast_memory_graph` — **Browser**

Returns a multi-character "cast graph" scoped to one conversation — every
character in that conversation's cast (gallery mains + NPCs) plus their
combined memories/links. Additive to (not a replacement for) the existing
per-character `get_memory_graph`, which spans all of one character's
conversations instead of all characters in one conversation.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |

Returns `Result<MemoryGraph, MythicError>`

### `debug_run_npc_detection` — **Browser**

TEMPORARY Phase-A dev command — runs the NPC detection pipeline directly
and synchronously (unlike the real pipeline, which always runs as a
swallowed-error background task) so it can be exercised and verified
before it's wired into live chat. Remove once Phase B wires automatic
triggers into `commands::chat`.

| Argument | Type |

| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `aiResponse` | `String` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

(tts)=
## tts

Source: `src-tauri/src/commands/tts.rs`

### `tts_model_status`

Whether the Kokoro model + voice pack are already cached on disk. Pure
filesystem check — doesn't load the engine.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<TtsModelStatus, MythicError>`

### `tts_download_model`

Downloads the model + voice pack if not already cached, emitting
`tts-download-progress` events as it goes. A no-op (returns
immediately) if already downloaded — callers don't need to check
`tts_model_status` first.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `tts_preload_engine`

Warms the TTS engine in the background if the model's already
downloaded — called from the frontend on app start when TTS is enabled,
so the ~4-5s load cost is paid once, quietly, before the user's first
real interaction rather than stacked onto it. A no-op, not an error,
when the model isn't downloaded yet (nothing to preload) or the engine
is already loaded — safe to call unconditionally on every app launch.

No arguments.

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`

### `tts_list_voices` — **Browser**

Lists available voices — the built-in Kokoro pack when `provider_id` is
`None` (loading the engine first if needed, unchanged from before issue
#78), or a cloud provider's own catalog when `Some`.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `providerId` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<Vec<VoiceInfo>, MythicError>`

### `tts_set_character_voice` — **Browser**

Assigns (or clears, via `voice_id: None`) the voice a character speaks
with. `voice_provider_id: None` means the built-in Kokoro engine
(unchanged default); `Some(id)` routes through that cloud provider
instead — always set together, since a voice id from one provider's
catalog means nothing under a different one (see issue #78).

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `characterId` | `String` |
| `voiceId` | `Option<String>` |
| `voiceProviderId` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<Character, MythicError>`

### `tts_test_speak` — **Browser**

Synthesizes `text` immediately and returns WAV bytes — for a "preview
this voice" button in the character editor. Base64-encoded rather than
raw `Vec<u8>`: a plain `Vec<u8>` return still serializes as a JSON
array of numbers over Tauri IPC (3-5x the byte size in JSON text),
while base64 is ~1.33x — meaningfully cheaper for a payload that can be
several hundred KB.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `text` | `String` |
| `voiceId` | `String` |
| `providerId` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<String, MythicError>`

### `tts_replay_message`

Replays an already-saved chat message's voice, sentence by sentence —
emits one `tts-chunk` event per completed sentence (same event, same
shape, as the live-streaming path in `commands::chat::streaming`), so
the frontend's existing `ttsPlayback.ts` queue starts playing the first
sentence as soon as it's ready instead of waiting for the whole message.
Measured the difference directly: a 4-sentence, ~700-character message
took 42s end-to-end through `tts_test_speak`'s single-WAV-then-return
design (silence the entire time) versus first audible sound at ~8s here
(first sentence done), with the rest arriving progressively.

Fire-and-forget from the frontend's perspective — it doesn't need to
await this to know playback started; `ttsPlayback.ts`'s `isSpeaking`/
`currentMessageId` already track that live. Still returns `Result` so a
genuine failure (bad voice_id, engine not loaded) surfaces as an error
rather than silently doing nothing.

| Argument | Type |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | `String` |
| `messageId` | `String` |
| `text` | `String` |
| `voiceId` | `String` |
| `providerId` | `Option<String>` |

Returns `Result<(), MythicError>`
